notes: Lead profile: SMB, B2B SaaS (support chat widget embedded in client apps). Mostly self-serve onboarding; small ops team (2 infra, 1 frontend, 1 product).
Primary workload: low-latency chat for live agents + automated replies; secondary use: embedding-based doc search for KB articles.
Customer perf targets: p50 <200ms, p95 <500ms for chat path. Current observed: p50 ~320ms in EU, p95 spikes to >1.2s during peak.

Root causes discussed: region routing set to closest-network but defaulted to us-east-1 for some EU customers due to DNS routing; frontend SDK timeout set high (60s) causing slow retry semantics; prompts include full conversation history (~1600 tokens) each call.

Quick wins recommended by SE: 1) Pin EU traffic to eu-west-1 via explicit region parameter; 2) Enable streaming responses to render incremental tokens and reduce perceived latency; 3) Set client-side timeout to 10-15s with exponential backoff for retries; 4) Use prefix caching for stable system instructions; 5) Trim conversation history to 3 most-recent turns + compressed summaries (aim for <800 tokens per request).

SE notes: suggested model variants with lower context overhead and quantization-friendly options to lower per-token CPU time. Advised to test continuous-batching off for low-concurrency interactive flows.

Customer concerns: cost sensitivity on token retention (wants recommendations to avoid token bloat), needs simple config they can hand to frontend devs. No immediate VPC/on-prem need — ok with public cloud hosted API.
Quote from product lead: 'If we can get EU median under 250ms and p95 under 600ms we'll be comfortable moving to paid plan.'
Support artifacts: shared perf checklist (drive://redwood/marmalade/perf-checklist.md), suggested prompt templates and trimming examples in the drive deck.
Next technical asks from customer: sample timeout/retry code snippet for web SDK, region selection example, and a short list of prompt-length heuristics for chat widgets.
